claim_text: An unclassified CIA and ODNI system used for open-source intelligence analysis was breached
summary: CyberScoop, Nextgov/FCW, AP and CNN each report, citing their own unnamed sources, that hackers breached an unclassified system the CIA and ODNI use to analyse public and commercially available information.
detail: CyberScoop says it confirmed the breach with a source familiar with it; Nextgov/FCW cites two people familiar with the matter; AP one person familiar with the incident; CNN four sources familiar with the matter, and calls it an 'apparent hack'. None of the sources is named, and neither agency has confirmed the breach on the record.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Four outlets, each with its own sourcing, report the breach of an unclassified open-source intelligence system used by the CIA and ODNI.
notes: Confirms that the breach is reported by independent outlets, not what was reached or who did it.

claim_text: The CIA declined to comment; neither agency has confirmed the breach on the record
summary: The CIA declined to comment to CyberScoop, Nextgov/FCW and CNN. ODNI did not respond to CyberScoop or Nextgov/FCW. An ODNI official told CNN: 'There have been no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems.'
detail: The ODNI official's words, as CNN gives them, speak to classified systems and capabilities; they do not confirm or deny the breach. We found no official written statement on the incident.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Each outlet says the CIA declined to comment; CNN quotes the ODNI official.

claim_text: No classified systems or classified information were affected
summary: Sources told CyberScoop, AP and CNN classified networks and information were not affected. CyberScoop's source: 'The hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk.'
detail: This rests on unnamed sources and an unnamed ODNI official; nobody independent has examined it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: CyberScoop, AP and CNN each report that no classified information or systems were affected.

claim_text: What information was exposed, and when the breach happened, is not known
summary: AP says it was not clear what specific information was compromised. Nextgov/FCW says it is unclear whether any information was taken. CNN says it was not immediately clear when the hack occurred.
detail: CyberScoop's source said there was a disruption but the exposure was limited. The New York Times, which first reported the breach, is said by CyberScoop to have written that some unclassified information was exposed; we did not read the Times report.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources says what was taken or when the intrusion began.

claim_text: Early indications suggest the hack may have come from China; whether its government was involved is not clear
summary: CNN reports that two sources said early indications suggest the hack may have originated in China, though it was not immediately clear whether the country's government was involved.
detail: No government body has attributed the breach. Other outlets say it is unclear who carried it out.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: CNN cites two sources for the early indication.
notes: Single outlet, unnamed sources: Reported. Not an attribution.

claim_text: An AI-powered hacking tool called ARTEX is believed to have been used
summary: Nextgov/FCW reports that ARTEX, an AI tool that automatically finds and breaks into computer systems, is believed to have been used in the breach.
detail: Nextgov/FCW describes ARTEX as developed by a Chinese cybersecurity engineer and recently favoured by criminal hackers. A tool shared by many attackers does not identify who used it here.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Nextgov/FCW says ARTEX is believed to have been used.
notes: Single outlet: Reported. The engineer's online alias is left out.

summary: A person familiar with the incident told AP the issue has been resolved, and a second person told Nextgov/FCW the matter has been resolved. CNN says it was not immediately clear whether it has been resolved.
detail: The agencies have not said so themselves.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: AP and Nextgov/FCW each quote a person saying it has been resolved; CNN says it is unclear.

claim_text: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency was also affected
summary: Nextgov/FCW says The New York Times reported that the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) was affected at the same time as the CIA and ODNI.
detail: NGA did not immediately respond to Nextgov/FCW. We did not read the Times report.
label: Reported

claim_text: The breach does not appear to be related to the apparent FBI crime database hack
summary: Two of CNN's sources said the incident does not appear to be related to the apparent hack of the FBI's National Crime Information Center. CNN also says it is unclear whether the FinCEN cybersecurity incident is connected.
detail: AP and Nextgov/FCW place the breach after other federal incidents and outages, including the FBI database hack and the NSA network disruption, without linking them.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: CNN's two sources say it does not appear related; the other outlets draw no link.

claim_text: The New York Times first reported the breach on Tuesday Nov 24
summary: CyberScoop, AP and CNN each say The New York Times first reported the breach, on Tuesday Nov 24; the other outlets confirmed it the same day.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three outlets credit the Times with the first report on Tuesday.
notes: We did not read the Times report itself.
